# Sathya Sankaran

> Urban technologist and policy professional based in Bengaluru, India. CEO of Rainmatter Foundation. Co-Founder of Urban Morph (full-stack, AI-native urban-tech venture studio). Bicycle Mayor of Bengaluru, author of Break the Block (2026), host of OoruLabs podcast. Three decades at the intersection of code, public policy, and cities. Builder of AltMo (mobility intelligence) and SyntheSYS (AI urban intelligence). Founding-team member of Cycle Day, India's longest-running community-driven open-streets event.

## Identity

- Full name: Sathyanarayanan Sankaran

- Education: Bachelor's in Computer Science (Bangalore University) · Post Graduate Program in Public Policy (Takshashila Institution)

## Primary Affiliation

- **Rainmatter Foundation** (CEO). Thesis-based investing for urban sustainability, waste, energy transition, and sustainable materials. The mandate: build on the foundation's zero-to-one journey to shift places from resource-consuming to climate-conscious, participatory, resilient ones, and prepare alt-everything for the climate crisis that is upon us. Unlocking the alt-everything isn't a search problem, it's a thinking problem. https://rainmatter.org

## Other Roles

- **Urban Morph** (Co-Founder & Director). Full-stack, AI-native urban-tech venture studio in Bengaluru. Ships AltMo, SyntheSYS, and platforms across mobility, governance, and citizen engagement. https://www.urbanmorph.com
- **Bicycle Mayor of Bengaluru** (BYCS Amsterdam). Cycling infrastructure, road safety, and active mobility advocacy. https://bycs.org

- **Bioman Technologies**: circular-economy waste management

## Things Built or Co-Built

- [AltMo](https://www.altmo.app): GPS-verified mobility intelligence platform. Built at Urban Morph. Drove a 342% increase in cycling and walking infrastructure allocation in Bengaluru's Comprehensive Master Plan; helped establish 20+ km of dedicated cycle tracks; 500+ tonnes CO₂ avoided to date; 9,000+ users across 100+ cities and 900+ organisations.
- [SyntheSYS](https://www.urbanmorph.com/synthesys/): AI-powered urban intelligence platform. Built at Urban Morph. Ward to nation. Currently shipping dashboards for the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission, Neighbourhoods of the Future (https://notf.in), and digital information portals for businesses and public-good initiatives.
- [Break the Block](https://www.breaktheblock.in): Book (2026, Notion Press, ISBN 979-8-90269-374-1). "Twelve Lessons for Citizen-Led Change from Bengaluru's Rail Campaign." Distilled from a decade of the Namma Railu campaign that secured Union Cabinet approval for Bengaluru Suburban Rail in 2020.
- [OoruLabs Podcast](https://podcast.oorulabs.com): India's premier urban-affairs podcast. Long-form interviews with policymakers, planners, transit chiefs, civic activists, climate scientists, and international urbanists.
- [Relief Riders](https://www.cfam.in/reliefriders.html): COVID-19 cycling response. 725 volunteers across 12 Indian cities ferrying medicine, oxygen, and food. 2021 UN World Bicycle Day Special Award; 2022 Nobel Peace Prize Nomination.
- [mdshare](https://mdshare.live): Free, no-login markdown sharing. Open source. Multi-surface: browser, Obsidian, VS Code, plus MCP integrations for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI. Four permission tiers, threaded inline comments, real-time WebSocket sync, instant link revocation.
- [bharatlas](https://bharatlas.com): India's open atlas. 100+ map layers, free to explore: administrative boundaries from state to village, wards for 30+ cities, plus rivers, forests, highways, groundwater, floods, and seismic zones. Download as GeoJSON, Shapefile, Parquet, or PMTiles, or drop your own geo file and share it by link. Open licences, queryable from AI tools via MCP, no signup, no tracking.
- [Irrational](https://irrational.pages.dev): Decision-audit engine for cognitive biases. Describe a decision and it generates an adversarial prompt that argues the other side, refracting your choice through 22 biases (sunk cost, anchoring, overconfidence, and more). Your own AI runs the audit; nothing is stored. Works as an MCP tool. MIT licensed, no login.
- [Mugilu](https://mugilu.live): The open sky of India. Name any place and get the current air, heat, and hazards over it: CPCB AQI with pollutant breakdown and AQLI years of life lost, heat and wet-bulb stress, wind, fog, dust, crop-burn smoke (NASA FIRMS), UV, and live NDMA / IMD warnings. Search in Indian languages or use your location, no map needed. Data from CPCB, Open-Meteo, and NASA FIRMS. Open source, no login, queryable from AI tools via MCP.
- [twelveswaras](https://twelveswaras.com): Shazam for raagas. A browser tool that identifies Carnatic ragas from a short audio clip: hold your phone to the music and it returns the top three raga matches with confidence, detects the tonic (Sa) from the tanpura drone, and offers plain-language ear-training cues. Audio is analysed on the device and never stored. Free, no login, open source, released as a CC-BY non-commercial public good.
- [Overlooked](https://overlooked-india.pages.dev): India's species from every public source, in one list. Joins GBIF, iNaturalist, the Zoological Survey of India, the Botanical Survey of India, Kew and the IUCN Red List into one master list of species known from India: for each species and state, whether it has been observed, whether it has a confirmed identification, and its IUCN threat category, with a monthly feed of what changed. An experimental Shortlists page gives people who identify iNaturalist observations a short list of likely names from a model (BioCLIP 2.5 with a classifier trained on Indian research-grade photos); a person checks every name and nothing is posted to iNaturalist. Data CC BY 4.0, code MIT, no login.
- Cycle Day: India's longest-running community-driven open-streets event. 800+ events over 10 years, run by 80+ community partners. Founding-team member.

## Data Stories

Data-driven investigations published as standalone scrollytelling pieces:

- [The Overlooked Species](https://overlooked-species.surge.sh): A data story on what India records about its plants and animals, and what it leaves out. India has 6.38 crore public biodiversity records, and 96% are of birds, yet only 1,633 of the 49,398 species on record are birds. About 18,600 of India's 21,101 known beetle species have no public record with a location; flies, wasps and spiders show the same gap. Records follow observers, not forests: Kerala has 3,527 observations per 1,000 km², Madhya Pradesh, with the largest forest cover, has 61. For 59% of recorded moss and liverwort species there is no public record since 1980 (birds: 5%). The IUCN Red List has assessed 17% of India's native plants. For 84% of the 1,753 plants, fungi and related species described from India in 2015 to 2024, there is no public record of where they occur. India's registered collections hold about 95 lakh specimens, and fewer than 0.4% are online. A state map, and a comparison with nine other countries. Data from GBIF, iNaturalist, the Zoological and Botanical Surveys of India, Kew and the IUCN Red List. No login.
- [The Bill Arrives on Time](https://el-nino.surge.sh): A data story on El Niño and India's monsoon, written during the 2026 El Niño. El Niño is natural, always comes back, and is the one climate shock India sees coming 6 to 9 months ahead, yet the bill arrives in full. The 2026 monsoon came in at 87% of normal, the worst since 2015, while the Pacific ran +2.0°C warm through June to September, the most since at least 1950. Over 77 years, 9 of 15 El Niño summers ended in drought and none of 15 La Niña summers did; the Indian Ocean and the weather decide the rest. Each of the last three El Niño droughts (2002, 2009, 2015) cost ₹53,000 to ₹1,27,000 crore of kharif crops at today's support prices, and the 2026 bill is estimated at about ₹1.1 lakh crore (range ₹0.68 to 1.96 lakh crore) until official harvest numbers arrive. A state leaderboard combines rain-fed farmland and groundwater stress; Karnataka is hit both ways, with about 55% of its farmland rain-fed and 7 districts already pumping 90% or more of their recharge. The 2026 event began in May, NOAA declared it on 11 June, it will likely peak in October to December, and past strong El Niños suggest it ends around March to May 2027. Heat action plans return 14 to 123 times their cost in Indian cities. Data from NOAA, IMD, IITM, CGWB and DES, with maps from bharatlas. No login.
- [Land Ledger](https://land-ledger.surge.sh): A map-based compendium of India's land, district by district. It brings together seven earlier stories on soil, water, food and farmers, and asks one question of every field: what goes on, and what comes off. Calculated nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium balances (with 95% ranges), irrigation water use, measured water-table trends for 5,367 blocks, and soil carbon scenarios, each with a confidence flag. Finds that the harvest carries away about 48 of every 100 kg of nitrogen applied; that 57% of the potassium leaving fields goes out in straw; that soil-test labs disagree more than soils do (about 1.3x between districts of a state, 1.4x across states); and that more than half the blocks rated over-exploited show no clear fall in the water table. Every district links to the stories that cover it, and 197 districts link to CoRE Stack's tehsil-level Know Your Landscape models. No login.
- [Where India's Food Goes](https://same-heap.surge.sh): A data investigation into India's food system, following 1,590 million tonnes a year from the field to the plate. India grows 672 grams of cereal per person a day against an intake of 293 and a dietary guideline of 250; consumption has fallen for thirty years while the harvest climbed, and grain sits in godowns at three times the buffer norm. About a tenth of everything grown is never eaten, half lost before it leaves the farm and half thrown out by households. A dairy farmer keeps 70 paise of the retail rupee and a vegetable farmer about 35, a gap explained by the dairy cooperative rather than by the crop, and by a market in which no buyer can tell a careful lot from a careless one. All branded packaged food together is 2.9% of what the country processes, too small to be the problem or the fix. The central finding is that ownership decides who gets the money and not whether the soil and the aquifer survive: the Netherlands, where cooperatives handle about 70% of the market, is buying out farms over a nitrogen surplus, and the United States has drawn the Ogallala aquifer down by a tenth. India spends 42 rupees of fertiliser subsidy for every rupee given to the ministry handling food after harvest, and is short about 70,000 pack houses.
- [Upwind](https://upwind.surge.sh): A data investigation into the air and waste of the Delhi National Capital Region, built from a claims ledger of 165 rows across five states, each row carrying a source, a date and one of four evidence tags. Only 30 percent of Delhi's winter PM2.5 is made in Delhi; 83 percent of the secondary aerosol forms more than 30 kilometres away, and two models built years apart agree that no city-only measure reaches 35. Seven of the eleven coal plants within 300 km are exempt from sulphur controls under the July 2025 gazette and six of those seven sit upwind. Satellite fire counts fell 94 percent while burnt area fell 37 and most large fires are now lit after the satellite passes. The eight NCR districts around Delhi now register more vehicles a year than Delhi does, on 27 buses per lakh people against a national benchmark of 60. The pathway proposed is one annual airshed target per district published monthly, and a regional regulatory sandbox in which a new instrument runs under measurement for a fixed term, the process rule it suspends is named, and what moves the number becomes the rule across five states. Precedents measured abroad: Tokyo's 2003 diesel rule, written on driving rather than registration, and Hong Kong's enforcement on remote sensing.
- [Influence the Rule, Not the Bird](https://not-the-bird.surge.sh): A data story on emergence and the commons, for anyone in the non-profit space who funds, convenes, studies or does the work of protecting air, water, soil, biodiversity, energy or materials. Simple building blocks with simple rules produce a flock; money and effort mostly buy blocks and add speed, while direction is set by rules. Follows the idea through where climate finance actually goes, India's oldest budget lines, the solar auction, Sri Lanka's fertiliser ban against Hiware Bazar's water budget, and the border artefacts that let groups who disagree act together, with one example per asset and two still being tried. Principles: subsidiarity and place-based ownership.
- [The Question They Made Optional](https://made-optional.surge.sh): A data investigation into business and biodiversity in India. 786 of the country's biggest listed companies say in their filings that they operate in or beside ecologically sensitive places: national parks, wetlands, forests, coastlines. Only 33 said what they actually do there, with a location, a named impact and an outcome; the question was optional, so the rest broke no rule. Built on an IIM Bangalore study of 982 of India's top 1,000 listed companies' 2024-25 sustainability reports, set against the wider gap between how much the economy depends on nature and how little it measures or discloses.
- [The Best-Measured Soil in the World](https://dead-reckoning.surge.sh): A data investigation into India's Soil Health Card programme, the largest soil survey on Earth: over 5 million samples a year, twelve measurements each, going back a decade. More than half of India's farmland reads low on organic carbon, yet with no independent reference to calibrate against, the readings navigate by dead reckoning. Examines what the card measures and what it misses, and why 71% of a 1.68 lakh crore fertiliser subsidy still goes to urea.
- [The Register No One Reads](https://pbr-story.surge.sh): A data investigation into India's People's Biodiversity Registers. Conceived by Madhav Gadgil in 1996 to put villages in charge of documenting and governing their local nature, 2.72 lakh registers now exist on paper, yet only two have been formally approved. A story of coverage without empowerment: weak oversight, negligible public access, and community knowledge recorded but never acted on.
- [The Ground Beneath the Report Card](https://canitlast.surge.sh): A data investigation into rural India's sustainability. The official Panchayat Advancement Index grades 2.6 lakh villages on how they are doing today, not whether they can keep going. Rebuilds the score across three foundations, with draggable weights: land (groundwater, forests, glaciers, soil), economy (crop diversity and local wealth through FPOs and SHGs), and people (child stunting, maternal anemia, hospital births). Finds the northwest grain belt looks successful while spending its water fastest, while forested tribal regions rated "backward" prove more sustainable. No login.
- [The Uncounted](https://the-uncounted.surge.sh): A data investigation into human-wildlife conflict in India. Roughly 100,000+ conflict incidents a year across 88 species, yet national death counts are kept for only two. Argues the core problem is institutional inattention, not the species, and that the burden falls hardest on the poorest communities.
- [Whose Forest Is It?](https://whose-forest.surge.sh): A data investigation into India's Community Forest Rights. India mapped 3.46 crore hectares of community forest that local communities could govern; less than 3% has been recognised.
- [The Hollow Collective](https://fpo-story.surge.sh): The real state of India's Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), told through the data.
- [The Ground They Stand On](https://shg-story.surge.sh): India's nine crore women in self-help groups (SHGs), and the climb that still matters.
